notes: Accepted round-1 deviation (recorded, not failed): the ETag has three segments "<dayVersion>.<settingsVersion>.<flagBits>" (observed "0.68.11" and "2.68.11"), not the contract's literal two-segment shape.

Deviation from the parent's step-7 expectation: the counter ended at version 2, not 1. Explanation (design, not a defect of the clause): each withReservationWrite call bumps affected (locationId, businessDate) dates once, and the sibling unit test apps/tenant-api/src/routes/reservations-public.test.ts:378-400 asserts that a hold alone on a fresh date yields dayVersion 1. My flow was hold (0->1) then booking (1->2) = 2; rsv_day_versions.updated_at 1792264679397 equals the reservation created_at, so the last bump is the booking's. The clause under test (old ETag -> 200 + NEW ETag after a booking) holds either way.

frictions.description: The parent's step-7 expectation 'rsv_day_versions now holds version 1' for a hold+book flow is off by one: the hold itself is a versioned write (unit test reservations-public.test.ts:378-400 asserts dayVersion 1 after a hold alone on a fresh date), so hold+booking lands on 2.
frictions.resolution: Recorded observed version 2 with the raw row, the hold row (status converted), and the code/test citation that explains the arithmetic; did not treat it as an assertion failure.

summary: VAL-ONLINE-002 (ETag clause) PASSES on the fixed build. 2026-11-29 was a never-mutated date (0 rows in rsv_day_versions, dayVersion 0, ETag "0.68.11", 36 grid slots for party 2); the exact ETag replayed -> 304 with an empty body; after one hold + one booking (201 each) the same old-ETag conditional request returned 200 with a NEW ETag "2.68.11" and dayVersion 2, with the capacity change visible in the slot set; the new ETag replayed -> 304; read-only sqlite3 confirms the version row (2) and the booking row (rsv_f6032bd2-72fd-4ed4-a562-512ad28826da, 2026-11-29 10:00, party 2, booked). Two recorded deviations, neither a failure: the accepted three-segment ETag shape, and the version counter reaching 2 rather than the parent's expected 1 because the hold is itself a versioned write. No blockers; 2026-12-03 untouched and no services were started.
